summary: Vietnam has opened up corporate buying of clean power, with rooftop self-consumption and direct power purchase agreements now working and prices freely negotiated. Utility-scale investors face an unresolved dispute over feed-in tariffs for 173 operating projects.

access.reason: Feed-in tariffs have ended. New utility projects are chosen by investor selection, with the winning tariff capped at a regulated price ceiling.

terms.reason: Curtailment compensation and termination terms in new EVN contracts were not confirmed from a source we could read.

buyer.reason: Investors report EVN withheld part of payments and applied lower temporary tariffs to disputed feed-in tariff projects.

ownership.reason: Profits can be repatriated after notifying the tax authority, and foreign loans must be registered. Ownership caps for renewables were not confirmed.

build.reason: Investor guidance flags grid connection, congestion and curtailment as core risks for new projects.

stability.reason: EVN proposed in April 2026 transitional tariffs up to 43% below feed-in rates for 173 operating projects. No final decision found.

direction.reason: A ministry directive asked provinces to review the affected feed-in tariff projects, but no settlement had been published.

access.reason: Rooftop self-consumption is allowed, and DPPAs run by private line or through the grid. Physical DPPAs opened to buyers using 20,000 kWh a month.

terms.reason: DPPA prices, physical or through the grid, may now be freely negotiated.

ownership.reason: Profits can be repatriated after notifying the tax authority, and foreign loans must be registered. Ownership caps were not confirmed.

build.reason: Investor guidance flags grid connection and curtailment as core risks, and rooftop surplus sales are capped at 50% of output.

stability.reason: Rooftop and DPPA rules changed several times since 2024, mostly loosening, but the feed-in tariff dispute shows existing terms can be reopened.

direction.reason: Decree 243 of June 2026 raised the rooftop surplus sales cap from 20% to 50% and added data centres as grid DPPA buyers.

redFlags.reason: Payments to about 173 wind and solar projects were cut or delayed while their feed-in tariff eligibility is reviewed.
